memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'Now then, please let your servant remain here as my lord's slave in place of the boy, and let the boy return with his brothers. How can I go back to my father if the boy is not with me? No! Do not let me see the misery that would come on my father.'" — Gen 44:33-34 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
"Let your servant remain here as my lord's slave in place of the boy."

Here it is — the sentence the whole chapter has been building towards. Judah, who once sold a brother into slavery for silver, now offers to become a slave himself so that a brother can go free. The man who created the family's greatest wound is offering his own life to heal it.

This is the fruit of genuine repentance, and it is one of the most moving moments in the Old Testament. Judah is not making excuses, not bargaining, not asking for leniency. He is asking to take the punishment himself.

And from this man's tribe, generations later, would come the Lion of the tribe of Judah (Rev 5:5) — who would do infinitely more than offer. Jesus actually took our place. He became a servant so we could become sons. He was bound so we could go free. He stayed under judgement so we could go home to the Father.

Judah could not save Benjamin by his offer; Joseph was about to reveal himself and no substitution was needed. But Christ's substitution was real, accepted, and complete. Because He took your place, there is nothing left for you to pay.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. How does Judah's offer help you feel the weight of what Jesus did for you?
2. Where is God calling you to lay down your own comfort for someone else?
3. Have you personally accepted that Christ took your place?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord Jesus, You took my place. You were bound so that I could go free, and You bore what I could never have carried. Thank You. Let my life be a thank-you to You. Amen.
